title: Why Beijing May Favor a “Slow and Steady” Rise For its Currency - The Wire China
gist: Paywalled teaser arguing Beijing may prefer a gradual 'slow and steady' renminbi appreciation amid a record trade surplus likely over $1.2 trillion this year and mounting global calls for rebalancing and currency revaluation.

insights.claim: China's trade surplus is the largest in world history and likely over $1.2 trillion this year.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: An unprecedented surplus raises odds of coordinated trade protection and currency pressure on Beijing.
insights.quote: Amid the largest trade surplus in world history — likely over $1.2 trillion this year

insights.claim: Calls for Chinese policymakers to rebalance the economy toward domestic demand are growing louder as China's export success provokes anxiety among trading partners.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Rebalancing pressure could shift Chinese policy toward consumption stimulus, relevant for consumer and import plays.
insights.quote: calls for Chinese policymakers to ‘rebalance’ the economy towards domestic demand are growing louder

insights.claim: Surging goods imports from China are pushing global policymakers to consider or enact various forms of trade protection.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Expanding tariffs and anti-dumping measures globally pose margin risk for Chinese exporters.
insights.quote: With goods imports from China surging, global policymakers are considering, or have enacted, various forms of trade protection.

insights.claim: Beijing is likely to favor a gradual, slow and steady appreciation of the renminbi rather than a sharp revaluation in response to external pressure.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Implies a managed, low-volatility CNY appreciation path, favoring carry-style or gradual long-CNY positioning over bets on a step revaluation.
